simple.meaning: רֶגֶל (regel) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a foot (as used in walking); by implication, a step ; by euphemistically the pudenda.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 8:9. The surrounding context includes land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֶגֶל (H7272) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news came about Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse picked him up and fled. As she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

David commanded his young men, and they killed them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth, and buried it in Abner’s grave in Hebron.
The king said, “Is there not yet any of Saul’s house, that I may show the kindness of God to him?”
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem; for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.
Now in all Israel there was no one to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.
The king went out, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.
